scenes.title: Key ideas
scenes.vo: First, Floating rates: lending and borrowing APYs that change with utilisation (Module 3). Next, Fixed rates: PTs (10.1), fixed-rate lending markets and fixed-rate borrowing (#22). Then, Term structure: P.T. implied yields across maturities form a yield curve (for example 3-month versus 12-month). Upward sloping: the market expects rates to stay high or rise. Inverted: it expects them to fall. Also, Positioning: buying P.T. = receiving a fixed rate (you win if floating rates fall). Buying Y.T. = receiving the floating rate (you win if floating rates rise). Fixed-rate borrowing equals paying a fixed rate (you win if floating borrow rates rise). And finally, Basis between venues: the same asset's rates can differ across protocols and chains; the gap reflects risk, liquidity and friction as much as opportunity.
scenes.cap: First, Floating rates: lending and borrowing APYs that change with utilisation (Module 3). Next, Fixed rates: PTs (10.1), fixed-rate lending markets and fixed-rate borrowing (#22). scenes.title: Worked example
steps: You need the money in 12 months and think rates will fall
If you think rates will rise instead, stay floating (supply to lending) or…
scenes.vo: Let's work an example, step by step. Stablecoin P.T. implied yields: 3-month 7%, 12-month 9%. You need the money in 12 months and think rates will fall: buy the 12-month P.T. and lock 9%. If you think rates will rise instead, stay floating (supply to lending) or buy Y.T. with a small, capped amount.
